description: B2 WALLS, NO OPENINGS, 16 in o.c. (STUD-WALL; docs/reference-parts/buildings.md B2): FOUR loft.wall 1.0.0 custom features, drawn clockwise in plan with the framing to the right of each wall's direction (its line the exterior face): front from (144, 0) at 180 deg, 144 long; left side from (0, 3.5) at 90 deg, 113; back from (0, 120) at 0 deg, 144; right side from (144, 116.5) at 270 deg, 113; everything else the plugin's defaults (2x4 at 16 in o.c., 97.125 plate to plate, double SPF top plate, pressure-treated southern pine bottom plate, SPF studs). model.json is EXACTLY the four expansions with the member materials documents applies (each member body's material as a per-body assignment: no part default); members.json is each body's member metadata. packages/loft-plugins/tests/test_wall.py asserts both files are the plugin's output; services/geometry/tests/test_walls_b2.py checks the cut list, the exported STEP and interference. Each member is a plan rectangle on an XY level datum extruded up as a new body.
derivation: Every expectation except the mesh counts is ANALYTIC, from buildings.md's coordinates in exact rational arithmetic (x 25.4 = mm exactly), never from the plugin. Front plates X 0..144, Y 0..3.5; back X 0..144, Y 116.5..120; left X 0..3.5, Y 3.5..116.5; right X 140.5..144, Y 3.5..116.5. Bottom plate Z 0..1.5, top plates Z 94.125..95.625 and 95.625..97.125, studs Z 1.5..94.125 (92.625).

Stud centres from each wall's start at 0.75, then every 16, an end stud flush: a 144 wall 0.75, 16, ..., 128, 143.25 (10), a 113 wall 0.75, 16, ..., 96, 112.25 (8); 36 studs, 1.5 along the wall and 3.5 across it.
surface_area = sum of 2(ab + bc + ca) over the 48 boxes (bodies are separate, touching faces are not merged) = 49 269 in^2 = 31786388.04 mm^2.
centroid = volume-weighted mean of the box centres (exact rationals): x = 72 in = 1828.8 mm and y = 60 in = 1524.0 mm (the shed is symmetric about both), z = 2753267/52016 in = 1344.4513572746848 mm.

mass_g = (SPF volume x 450 + PT volume x 582) kg/m^3: bottom plates 2 x 144 + 2 x 113 = 514 in x 5.25 = 2 698.5 in^3 of PT, the rest SPF = 194628.065291478 g; center_of_mass x = 1828.8, y = 1524.0, z = 619756467/12065456 in = 1304.7011453027553 mm (the denser bottom plates pull it down).
topology: 48 boxes x (6 faces, 12 edges, 1 shell) = 288 faces, 576 edges, 48 shells.
MESH counts are recorded but also exact for boxes: 12 triangles and 24 vertices per box = 576 triangles, 1152 vertices.
tolerance_rationale: Measured first, then set (geometry-gates skill): the bounds are ABSOLUTE and the part is ~4e8 mm^3, so the double-precision sum of its separate bodies carries round-off near the ULP of the sum (~6e-8): measured 1.2e-7 mm^3 on the volume, 0 on the area, <= 7e-13 mm on the centroid and centre of mass, 1.2e-10 g on the mass (worst of both spacings: 2.4e-7 on the volume). 1e-6 is 4x the worst and ~3e-15 relative; a stud 0.001 in out of place moves the volume by >= 1.2 mm^3 and fails by six orders of magnitude.
roundtrip_tolerance_rationale: Measured 2026-10-17: the STEP round trip re-sums the re-imported solids in another order and moves the VOLUME by 2.4e-7 mm^3 and the AREA by 3.7e-9 mm^2 (~1e-15 relative), above ROUNDTRIP_TOL (1e-7 absolute), which is near the ULP of a 4e8 sum. 1e-6 is 3.3x the worst of the two spacings (3.0e-7). Same cause as b1-deck-framing-16ft and plugin-deck-v1-b1-12x16ft; it applies to volume and area only, centroid and bounds keep ROUNDTRIP_TOL.
